lines: Increasingly selective eating habits with recent weight loss and food rigidity

The patient, a 4-year-old male with Hirschsprung disease, cystic fibrosis, and metastatic neuroblastoma, returns for evaluation of feeding concerns following prior encounters for poor weight gain and constipation.
The parents report that their son has become increasingly selective with foods over the past six months, only accepting white bread and apple juice.
They also note that he has become irritable when presented with new foods and has difficulty transitioning between activities.
His growth chart shows a drop from the 50th to the 25th percentile for weight over this period.

The child was born at term without complications and met all developmental milestones on time until recently; his parents now report that he seems less interested in interactive play and has not been acquiring new words.
